title: Impact of Catalytic Converter Mandate on NOx Emissions

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

This is a classic DID setup. We have:
- **Treatment group**: Regions subject to the catalytic converter mandate (`treated = 1`)
- **Control group**: Regions without the mandate (`treated = 0`)
- **Pre/post periods**: Before and after mandate implementation (`post = 0/1`)
- **Interaction term**: `treat_x_post` captures the causal DID effect

The **key identifying assumption** is the **parallel trends assumption**: in the absence of the mandate, treated and control regions would have experienced the same trends in log NOx emissions. This is plausible if the control regions are comparable urban areas that were not subject to the policy change, and no other contemporaneous shocks differentially affected treated regions.

The DID estimator isolates the mandate's causal effect by differencing out both time-invariant regional differences and common time trends.

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# DID Analysis: Catalytic Converter Mandate on NOx Emissions
# ============================================================

library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# --- Load Data ---
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s47_data.csv")

cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
str(df)
cat("\nDimensions:", nrow(df), "rows x", ncol(df), "columns\n")
cat("\nSummary:\n")
print(summary(df))

# Check balance
cat("\n=== Group Sizes ===\n")
print(table(Treated = df$treated, Post = df$post))

# --- Group Means ---
cat("\n=== Group Means (Log NOx Emissions) ===\n")
group_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post, data = df, FUN = mean)
print(group_means)

# Manual DID calculation
mean_t1_post1 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 1])
mean_t1_post0 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 0])
mean_t0_post1 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 1])
mean_t0_post0 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 0])

did_manual <- (mean_t1_post1 - mean_t1_post0) - (mean_t0_post1 - mean_t0_post0)
cat("\n=== Manual DID Estimate ===\n")
cat("Treated, Post=1:", round(mean_t1_post1, 4), "\n")
cat("Treated, Post=0:", round(mean_t1_post0, 4), "\n")
cat("Control, Post=1:", round(mean_t0_post1, 4), "\n")
cat("Control, Post=0:", round(mean_t0_post0, 4), "\n")
cat("DID = (", round(mean_t1_post1, 4), "-", round(mean_t1_post0, 4), ") - (",
    round(mean_t0_post1, 4), "-", round(mean_t0_post0, 4), ")\n")
cat("DID Estimate (manual):", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")

# --- Main DID Regression ---
cat("\n=== Main DID Regression: y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post ===\n")
model1 <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
print(summary(model1))

# Robust standard errors (HC1)
cat("\n=== Robust Standard Errors (HC1) ===\n")
robust_se <- coeftest(model1, vcov = vcovHC(model1, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_se)

# --- Key Result ---
did_coef <- coef(model1)["treat_x_post"]
did_se <- sqrt(vcovHC(model1, type = "HC1")["treat_x_post", "treat_x_post"])
did_ci <- did_coef + c(-1.96, 1.96) * did_se

cat("\n============================================\n")
cat("  MAIN RESULT: DID Estimate (treat_x_post)\n")
cat("============================================\n")
cat("  Coefficient:", round(did_coef, 4), "\n")
cat("  Robust SE:  ", round(did_se, 4), "\n")
cat("  95% CI:     [", round(did_ci[1], 4), ",", round(did_ci[2], 4), "]\n")
cat("  t-stat:     ", round(did_coef / did_se, 4), "\n")
cat("  p-value:    ", round(robust_se["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"], 6), "\n")
cat("============================================\n")

# --- Robustness Check 1: Using the pre-built interaction vs manual ---
cat("\n=== Robustness Check 1: Manual interaction term ===\n")
df$interaction_manual <- df$treated * df$post
model2 <- lm(y ~ treated + post + interaction_manual, data = df)
cat("Coefficient on manual interaction:", round(coef(model2)["interaction_manual"], 4), "\n")
cat("Matches pre-built interaction:", 
    all.equal(coef(model1)["treat_x_post"], coef(model2)["interaction_manual"], 
              check.attributes = FALSE), "\n")

# --- Robustness Check 2: Unit fixed effects (if multiple periods per unit) ---
cat("\n=== Robustness Check 2: With unit fixed effects ===\n")
n_obs_per_unit <- table(df$unit_id)
if (any(n_obs_per_unit > 1)) {
  df$unit_id_factor <- as.factor(df$unit_id)
  model_fe <- lm(y ~ unit_id_factor + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
  cat("DID with unit FE:", round(coef(model_fe)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
  robust_fe <- coeftest(model_fe, vcov = vcovHC(model_fe, type = "HC1"))
  cat("Robust SE:", round(robust_fe["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"], 4), "\n")
  cat("p-value:", round(robust_fe["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"], 6), "\n")
} else {
  cat("Only one observation per unit-period; unit FE not estimable with this structure.\n")
  cat("Running with clustered-like robust SEs instead.\n")
}

# --- Robustness Check 3: Pre-treatment balance check ---
cat("\n=== Robustness Check 3: Pre-treatment balance ===\n")
pre_data <- df[df$post == 0, ]
pre_treat_mean <- mean(pre_data$y[pre_data$treated == 1])
pre_control_mean <- mean(pre_data$y[pre_data$treated == 0])
pre_diff_test <- t.test(y ~ treated, data = pre_data)
cat("Pre-treatment mean (treated):", round(pre_treat_mean, 4), "\n")
cat("Pre-treatment mean (control):", round(pre_control_mean, 4), "\n")
cat("Difference:", round(pre_treat_mean - pre_control_mean, 4), "\n")
cat("t-test p-value:", round(pre_diff_test$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("(This tests level differences, not trends - levels can differ in DID)\n")

# --- Interpretation ---
cat("\n=== Interpretation ===\n")
pct_change <- (exp(did_coef) - 1) * 100
cat("The mandate is associated with a", round(did_coef, 4), 
    "change in log NOx emissions.\n")
cat("This translates to approximately a", round(pct_change, 2), 
    "% change in NOx emission levels.\n")
if (did_coef < 0) {
  cat("The negative sign indicates the mandate REDUCED NOx emissions.\n")
} else {
  cat("The positive sign indicates the mandate INCREASED NOx emissions (unexpected).\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Negative.** Catalytic converters are specifically designed to reduce NOx emissions (along with CO and hydrocarbons) through chemical reduction reactions. A mandate requiring their installation should causally decrease NOx emissions in treated urban areas.

**Expected magnitude:** I expect the DID coefficient (`treat_x_post`) to be in the range of **-0.5 to -3.0 in log points**, corresponding to roughly a **40% to 95% reduction** in NOx emission levels. The actual magnitude depends on the baseline technology mix, compliance rates, and fleet turnover speed. Modern three-way catalytic converters can reduce NOx by 90%+ under ideal conditions, but real-world fleet-level effects would be smaller and phased in.

**Statistical significance:** Given the clear engineering mechanism, I expect the effect to be statistically significant (p < 0.05) if the sample has sufficient power. The `treated` coefficient may be positive or negative (reflecting pre-existing level differences between regions), and the `post` coefficient captures common time trends in emissions across all regions.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log NOx emissions between treated and untreated regions over time.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The catalytic converter mandate significantly reduces log NOx emissions.
